note: Every value is read from a CSV under results/. The main benchmark is a synthetic network study; confidence is a simulated proxy, not detector accuracy. The secondary detector study reports measured COCO recall and is labelled separately. Nothing here is a physical-robot or safety result.

paper.title: DAPPER: Deadline-Aware Edge Perception for Mission-Critical Robots under Dynamic Network Conditions
paper.affiliation: Al Ain University, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates

main.title: Repeated evaluation over 30 independent seeds
main.caption: 1,000 frames per seed, profile and policy at D = 100 ms. Intervals are 95% percentile bootstrap over seeds. The confidence proxy is the synthetic value the control loop holds at the deadline, not detector accuracy.

placement.title: DAPPER placement and remote accounting
placement.caption: At D = 100 ms over 30 seeds. Accepted is a percentage of transmitted requests; reuse and stale are percentages of all frames. Stale acceptance is zero by construction and measured so the claim is checked rather than asserted.

adaptive.title: DAPPER against the calibrated adaptive comparators and the offline oracle
adaptive.caption: Averaged over the five profiles at D = 100 ms. Each comparator's hyperparameters were fitted on the calibration seeds with the same objective used for DAPPER. The oracle reads the realised frame outcome and is not deployable.

ablation.title: One-at-a-time ablation
ablation.caption: Averaged over the five profiles and 30 seeds. Removing a risk signal sets its weight to zero and renormalises the remainder. No ablated variant produced a nonzero deadline-miss rate.

detector.title: Measured detector quality on all 5,000 COCO val2017 images
detector.caption: Confidence threshold 0.25, IoU matching at 0.50. Safety-relevant classes are person, bicycle, car, motorcycle, bus and truck. Measured on one workstation; not embedded or robot timing.

replay.title: Detection quality delivered when the measured detector outputs are replayed
replay.caption: D = 100 ms, 10 seeds, synthetic network profiles. “all” scores a reused output as detecting nothing, which is a lower bound because consecutive COCO images are unrelated; “fresh” averages only freshly computed outputs. Both are reported rather than choosing whichever is more favourable.

honest.headline: All-frame delivered recall falls below local-only where DAPPER reuses
honest.explanation: A reused output is scored as detecting nothing in the current image. Consecutive COCO validation images are unrelated, so this is a lower bound a real video stream would not incur; the fresh-frame column shows no such gap. Both views are reported.

honest.headline: Bandwidth is the price, and a large share of it buys nothing
honest.explanation: Every transmitted request is charged its upload bandwidth even when the packet is lost or the reply arrives too late to accept. Under stable conditions roughly half the traffic, and under lossy conditions the large majority, returns no usable result.
honest.paper_ref: Table III, Table IV, Sec. V-B

honest.headline: The frozen 100-ms calibration is not reliable at every larger deadline
honest.explanation: Parameters were selected at D = 100 ms, where no frame enters edge-accurate, so the commit margin m is unidentifiable there. At larger deadlines frames do commit, and the calibrated m = 0.80 produces misses. The zero-miss result is scoped to D = 100 ms; multi-deadline calibration is the remedy.
